title: Dedicated capacity: Isolation modes and burst governance PRD
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: High-level product requirements and acceptance criteria for adding fine-grained isolation modes and burst governance to Redwood Dedicated. This PRD defines the functional surface for capacity isolation (soft vs hard), idle/burst queue policies, burst windows and throttling, admin controls in the Console, API surfaces for programmatic policy controls, billing/metrics implications, and required auditability for compliance customers.
background: Customers running regulated or multi-tenant workloads on Dedicated have asked for clearer isolation guarantees and predictable burst behaviors. Current Reserved Pools provide capacity reservation and a simple burst toggle; customers need: (1) explicit isolation modes to control noisy neighbors, (2) governable burst windows (how long bursts can run and how often), (3) queueing/backpressure policies when capacity is exhausted, and (4) observability and audit trails for policy changes. This initiative aims to reduce customer support load, enable enterprise adoption in regulated industries, and improve platform predictability.
goals: Introduce two isolation modes: 'Soft Isolation' (resource prioritization + best-effort eviction) and 'Hard Isolation' (dedicated vGPU slices with strict network/data isolation), controllable per reserved pool
Provide burst governance: configurable burst_window_seconds, burst_credits, cooldown_period, and per-pool burst_max_qps to limit unbounded spiky traffic
Add queueing and fallback policies: FIFO queue, priority queue (per-token priority), or immediate rejection with configurable HTTP 429 payloads
Surface admin controls in Redwood Console for policy creation, simulation, and audit logs; expose same controls via API/SDK
Emit metrics and events needed for billing accuracy, SLO dashboards, and compliance audit (policy change events, eviction events, burst usage metrics)
non_goals: Not enabling arbitrary tenant-level hypervisor configuration or custom kernel builds (out of scope for this cycle)
Not implementing new hardware placement algorithms — we'll rely on existing scheduler and enforce isolation at pool allocation boundaries
Not building a full AI-driven predictive autoscaler in this phase; minimal predictive scaling integration is scoped as an MVP feature toggle
requirements_functional: Admin APIs: PATCH /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/policies to set isolation_mode (soft|hard), burst_window_seconds, burst_credits, cooldown_period_seconds, burst_max_qps, queue_policy (fifo|priority|reject)
Console UI: Pool settings page must provide a policy editor, a 'simulate burst' sandbox button that runs a dry run and reports expected throttling/queueing results

Isolation behavior: Soft Isolation must deprioritize cross-pool requests via scheduler weights; Hard Isolation must map to VPC-level isolation and reserved hardware allocation with no eviction for pinned instances
Burst accounting: system must track burst_credits consumed per-pool and reset after cooldown_period; exceedances must be logged and emit an alert event
Queueing: when queueing enabled, the request router must return spike-time estimates and position in queue via streaming headers, and must support configurable maximum queue length
Auditability: every policy change must create an immutable audit entry including actor, timestamp, previous policy, and reason; entries must be queryable via API
Billing integration: burst consumption metrics must be exported to billing pipeline as a separate meter (dedicated_burst_units) for correct invoicing
requirements_nonfunctional: Latency SLO: soft isolation should not degrade p95 token latency by more than 15% for in-pool traffic under typical loads
Scalability: policy evaluation in the request path must add less than 1ms median overhead at 2000 rps
Reliability: disable path for burst governance must have a safe default (off) and fail-open behavior that returns HTTP 503 with clear diagnostics when policy store unreachable
Security: audit entries must be encrypted at rest and integrated with existing KMS keys used by Dedicated customers
Observability: emit metrically tagged timeseries for burst_credits, cooldown_remaining_seconds, queue_length, evictions_count with per-pool labels
ux_changes: Add 'Isolation & Burst' tab to each Dedicated Pool page in Redwood Console. Provide inline help, recommended defaults, a 'preview impact' modal that simulates a 5-minute spike, and an 'apply' flow that requires a two-step confirmation for Hard Isolation (because it may trigger hardware moves). Provide a policy history timeline with links to audit records.
api_changes: Public REST endpoints: GET/PUT/PATCH /v1/dedicated/pools/{id}/policies, GET /v1/dedicated/pools/{id}/policy-audit?since=YYYY-MM-DD. SDK bindings in JS/Python to wrap these endpoints. Add new telemetry events to /v1/telemetry/events for: policy.change, burst.consumed, pool.eviction. Document new error codes (429.BURST_LIMIT, 503.POLICY_UNAVAILABLE).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Create/Update policy: An admin can create and update a policy via Console and API; updates appear in the audit log with actor and timestamp

2) Isolation enforcement: In a lab, configure Soft Isolation and Hard Isolation pools and demonstrate that cross-pool noisy traffic affects Soft pools (lowered priority) but cannot evict Hard pools; provide test run artifacts (load test results and scheduler traces)

3) Burst governance functioning: Configure burst_window_seconds=300, burst_credits=1e6 and demonstrate during a controlled spike that burst_credits decrease appropriately, cooldown is respected, and excess requests are queued or rejected per policy
4) Queueing headers: When requests are queued, client receives X-Queue-Position and X-Queue-Estimate headers and can stream the queue progress; integration test validates header presence and values
5) Metrics and billing: Telemetry for dedicated_burst_units emits per-pool metrics; billing pipeline ingests those metrics and a simulated invoice includes burst usage line items
6) Console UX: Policy editor modal passes accessibility checks, simulation results are displayed for a sample spike, and Hard Isolation apply triggers the two-step confirmation with clear warnings
7) Error handling: If policy store becomes unavailable, new requests receive documented 503.POLICY_UNAVAILABLE with UX indicating fallback behavior; system gracefully recovers when store is back
8) Security: Audit entries are present, encrypted at rest, and retrievable via API for the last 13 months (or customer retention window); automated test verifies encryption flag and KMS key usage
9) Performance: End-to-end median policy evaluation added latency is <=1ms and p95 token latency increase for in-pool traffic under test is <15%
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal Redwood tenants + 3 pilot customers (security review beforehand) — feature behind org toggle; collect qualitative feedback
Beta: broader set of Dedicated customers with default Soft Isolation enabled on new pools; monitor metrics and SLOs for 4 weeks
GA: enable in Console for all Dedicated customers; provide migration docs and recommended defaults. Announce in release notes and customer success playbooks
notes: Trade-offs considered: We debated supporting soft eviction callbacks to tenants (allowing in-app graceful degradation) but deferred until after pilot due to complexity and risk surface.
Open question: For Hard Isolation, do we charge a hardware reservation premium? Pricing team to propose model by 2025-03-20.
